claims.claim: An answer must contain a statement of any new matter constituting a defense.
claims.quote:
(b) The answer to a complaint shall contain:
(1) The general or specific denial of the material allegations of the complaint controverted by the defendant.
(2) A statement of any new matter constituting a defense.

claims.claim: The defenses must be separately stated.
claims.quote: The defenses shall be separately stated,

claims.claim: The defenses must refer to the causes of action they answer.
claims.quote: the several defenses shall refer to the causes of action which they are intended to answer, in a manner by which they may be intelligibly distinguished.
claims.note: The reference must make clear which defense answers which cause of action.

claims.claim: A general denial only puts in issue the material allegations of the complaint.
claims.quote: If the complaint is subject to Article 2 (commencing with Section 90) of Chapter 5.1 of Title 1 of Part 1 or is not verified, a general denial is sufficient but only puts in issue the material allegations of the complaint.
claims.note: The draft states the effect of a general denial but omits the conditions on its sufficiency and the exception for verified claims assigned for collection.

claims.claim: An action upon a contract founded upon an instrument in writing must be brought within four years.
claims.quote:
Within four years:
(a) An action upon any contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing, except as provided in Section 336a;
claims.note: Four years is the general period. Subsection (a) also limits certain actions for a secured balance to three months after a sale under a power of sale.

flags.text: A reader could rely on a general denial for a verified complaint on a claim assigned to a third party for collection. Section 431.30(d) requires denials made positively or according to information and belief in that situation, even if Article 2 applies.
The unqualified four-year statement omits the Section 336a exception and could cause a reader to overlook the shorter post-sale deadline in Section 337(a).

result.summary: Section 431.30 supports the three defense-pleading requirements. The general-denial and four-year statements omit qualifications that can change the practical answer.
